# Following instructions for a Tobit on http://www.ats.ucla.edu/stat/r/dae/tobit.htm
# My CSV was attached in the last email
# knitr and ggplot2
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
TobitTimeH3 <- read.csv("DissTimeChapterAnalysisH3RTobit.csv")
# function that gives the density of normal distribution for given mean
# and sd, scaled to be on a count metric for the histogram: count =
# density * sample size * bin width
f <- function(x, var, bw = 15) {dnorm(x, mean = mean(var), sd(var)) * length(var) * bw}
# Plot PctWeakTikes as the independent variable and NR_score as the dependent variable
p <- ggplot(TobitTimeH3, aes(x = PctWeakTies, fill = NR_score))
# Attempt to obtain the first histogram and the subsequent error message

p + stat_bin(binwidth = 1) + stat_function(fun = f, size = 1, args = list(var = TobitTimeH3$PctWeakTies, bw = 1))
Error in unit(tic_pos.c, "mm") : 'x' and 'units' must have length > 0

Thanks

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Don't know why I'm receiving units>0 error message running Tobit
parts:
Hi:

After looking at Josh's nicely done example at the UCLA site, I made a
couple of changes to your code; in particular, your bandwidth needs to
be reduced because the response ranges from 0 to 1. If you set the
bandwidth to 1, you'll only get one or two histogram bars and it's
pointless to draw a density plot over it.

p <- ggplot(TobitTimeH3, aes(x = PctWeakTies, fill = factor(NR_score)))
p + stat_bin(binwidth = 0.1) +

args = list(var = TobitTimeH3$PctWeakTies, bw = 0.1))

NR_score was converted to a factor; once that was done, the error
message disappeared. However, I wonder about the purpose of using 12
distinct fill colors in a single histogram. Perhaps some form of
aggregation of scores is in order (see the cut() function).

Dennis
